b: Talking creates the illusion of action. But leaders translate talk into results.
Evaluate your conversations by what happens afterwards.
Describe a desirable future. Explain why it matters.
Your announcement isn’t automatically their vision.
Brilliant ideas are dim until people see the light.
What does this mean to you?
Participation builds ownership. People support what they help shape.
A nodding head isn’t a commitment.
Leaders love launching initiatives. It takes work to track progress.
Completion creates confidence for the next challenge.
Getting stuff done requires four conversations.
At the beginning, build vision together.
During confusion, have an understanding conversation.
When following through lags, clarify commitments.
When projects linger, have a closure conversation.
The wrong conversation runs in circles.
Which of the four conversations do leaders most often neglect?
